articles.title: The best e-readers for every kind of bookworm, including note takers and people who never have a bag
articles.summary: NBC Selected editors tested popular e-readers from Amazon Kindle, Rakuten Kobo and more. Shop our favorite black-and-white, color and note-taking options.
articles.body: Hardcover books are great until you’re lugging three of them in a tote bag or squinting at a paperback under a dim lamp. An e-reader fits a whole library into something lighter than a single paperback, and it goes wherever you do: a morning commute, the beach, the couch, a crowded airplane cabin. And even though you aren’t flipping actual pages, many e-readers do what they can to feel like a real book. Most e-readers use an e-ink screen, which mimics the look of ink on paper, says Nick Tanzi, assistant director of the South Huntington Public Library. It’s easier on the eyes than the LCD screen you find in tablets and uses far less battery, he adds. E-readers are also lighter than tablets, easier to carry than hardcovers and can hold thousands of ebooks. And because most don’t run other apps, they can cut down on distracting notifications, says Ramesh Mantha*, senior vice president of product at Rakuten Kobo, where he designs and builds e-readers. Below, I rounded up the best e-readers based on expert guidance and NBC Selected staff picks. *Mantha did not provide any specific product recommendations for this piece; the Kobo models featured on our list were chosen independently and without this expert’s influence. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best e-readers in 2026 Most of the below picks come from the two biggest e-reader brands: Amazon Kindle and Rakuten Kobo. Many are also regularly used by NBC Selected staffers. Best overall Amazon’s latest 6-inch Kindle is its smallest e-reader to date. It’s slimmer and lighter than the last version, and the screen now sits flush with the edges, so it slips easily into a jacket pocket or small bag. The 16GB of storage holds thousands of books, and the battery lasts up to six weeks between charges. Books also load about 30 percent faster than on the previous model, so you can get back to your story quicker. Amazon made it with recycled materials, including a battery built with 100 percent recycled cobalt. NBC Selected contributing writer Maria Cassano tested this Kobo Libra color e-reader after the brand sent her one, and it’s now one of her favorite gadgets. The color touchscreen is sharp and detailed, so book covers, illustrations and notes stand out more than they would on a black-and-white e-reader. Cassano also loves the physical page-turning buttons. Because you don’t have to tap the screen to turn the page, you’re less likely to highlight a word or open a link by accident, she says. You can pair it with the Kobo Stylus 2 (sold separately) for comfortable annotating and note taking, and keep both together in the Kobo Libra SleepCover Case with Stylus. Best for comfort The 2026 Kindle Paperwhite is Amazon’s most premium Paperwhite yet. Its thinner, flush 7-inch glare-free display offers the highest contrast of any Paperwhite, while an auto-adjusting front light keeps pages comfortable day or night. A double-tap feature to turn pages, dock charging, 32GB of storage, no lockscreen ads, IPX8 waterproofing, and up to 12 weeks of battery make it a standout among e-readers. Best Kindle alternative If you are looking for an alternative to an Amazon e-reader, this is the one to get. It’s Kobo’s lowest-priced e-reader and is very similar to a Kindle, with a glare-free black and white screen design that’s perfect for reading text. Like a Kindle, it is lightweight and portable, perfect for travel and vacation, especially with its weeks-long battery life. You purchase ebooks from the Rakuten Kobo store and can also rent books from your local library with the built-in Libby/Overdrive app — this is one of the things that differentiates it from Kindle. It’s also IPX8 waterproof, so you don’t have to worry when you bring it to the pool or the beach. You can also get the Kobo Clara in a colour version, the Kobo Clara Colour, but that version is pricier. The Boox Palma 2 is former NBC Selected commerce editor Jordan Bowman’s go-to device for reading everything. Note, this is not a traditional e-reader — it’s more like a minimalist phone with an e-ink style black and white display. That means you can do almost anything you would do on your phone (TikTok included), though the screen is better suited for reading. Bowman’s favorite part of the Palma 2 is its flexibility: it isn’t tied to one ebook store — you can download and read content from almost any app, Kindle, Kobo, Libby, Shonen Jump, Pocket, NBC News, you name it. Plus it’s much smaller than most traditional e-readers, you can actually fit it in your pocket, just like a smartphone. Best for note taking If you want your e-reader to pull double-duty as a note-taking machine, consider the Kindle Scribe. Former NBC Selected production coordinator Kelsey Fredricks tested a previous version of this e-reader for two months, and loved how it served as more than just an e-reader. The newest Scribe has a super responsive screen that is great for note taking — just use the included Scribe Premium Pen. The Scribe comes with extra features for note taking, things like templates to start with, folders to organize your files, and tools to send files to and from the Scribe for annotating, printing or emailing. Keep in mind that it is larger and heavier than the other e-readers we recommend. How I picked the best e-readers I combined expert advice with NBC Selected editors experience using e-readers daily to narrow down what makes an e-reader great. When determining the top picks, I kept the following in mind: Screen: The screen size and the resolution are the most important features to consider, as they directly impact your reading experience, according to our experts.Storage: Storage capacity for e-readers is measured in gigabytes (GB), and the larger the number, the more titles the device can hold. Graphic novels, comics and other books with illustrations often take up more storage than a standard e-book.Battery life: Unlike tablets, e-readers can often last weeks between charges, but larger screens and additional features may drain the battery faster.Store access: Typically, e-reader manufacturers only let you purchase ebooks through their brand’s compatible storefronts. For example, if you have a Kindle, you can only purchase ebooks through the Amazon store. How to shop for an e-reader When choosing the right e-reader for your needs, experts recommend keeping the following criteria in mind: Screen size “The most important feature of an e-reader is its screen,” says Mantha. E-reader screens are measured diagonally in inches from the top corner to the opposite bottom corner, and a large screen with easy-to-read text is preferred. Keep in mind that especially big screens aren’t as portable and may drain the battery faster, according to experts. Resolution Higher resolutions (measured in PPI, or pixels per inch) translate to crisper text, which is easier on the eyes, according to our experts. Lower resolutions, on the other hand, can result in a blurry reading experience, says Tanzi. All of the e-readers on our list have a PPI of 300 for black and white content. Storage Like most other devices, e-reader storage is measured in GB — the higher the number, the more books your device can store locally. Ebooks are generally small files, meaning that an e-reader can store hundreds, if not thousands of titles, says Tanzi. Keep in mind that picture books, graphic novels and other visual media take up substantially more storage space. For reference, 32GB of storage can hold up to 24,000 ebooks, according to Kobo. Battery Most e-readers last for weeks between charges. However, certain features like bright backlights and note-taking may drain the battery faster, and brands’ advertised battery life always varies depending on use. Store access Different e-reader manufacturers allow access to different e-book stores, and not all e-books are available on all storefronts. For example, Kindle allows users to purchase e-books through the Amazon store, while Kobo devices use the Kobo bookstore. Some devices let you transfer e-book files from your computer to your e-reader. Kindle vs. Kindle Paperwhite The Amazon Kindle and Amazon Kindle Paperwhite are two of the most popular e-readers you can buy. But it can be hard to tell them apart at a glance — they look almost identical in online photos. The Amazon Kindle Paperwhite is essentially an upgraded Amazon Kindle. It’s a little larger, has a sleeker design, gets double the battery life (12 weeks), is IPX8 waterproof and has an adjustable color temperature. The regular Amazon Kindle, by contrast, is smaller, gets only six weeks of battery life, isn’t waterproof and lacks the ability to adjust the color temperature. It is much less expensive, however. Reading on both devices is similar, as they both run the same software and have the same Kindle bookstore. If you can afford it, we highly recommend the Kindle Paperwhite over the regular Kindle. Being able to adjust the color temperature or warm light of the screen is a big deal: it makes reading in dark environments much easier on your eyes, in our experience. IPX8 waterproofing is also a huge peace of mind feature — you can read the Paperwhite by the pool, at the beach or in the bathtub without worry. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Meet our experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Nick Tanzi is the assistant director of the South Huntington Public Library.Ramesh Mantha is the senior vice president of product at Rakuten Kobo, where he designs and builds e-readers.* *The inclusion of Kobo products in this article was made independently of Mantha. Why trust NBC Selected? Harry Rabinowitz is a former reporter at NBC Selected who covers fitness and technology including guides to smartwatches, fitness trackers and over-ear headphones. He’s been covering and testing e-readers for years. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok to stay up to date.

articles.title: Home secretary plans to tackle 'perception of two-tier policing'
articles.summary: Shabana Mahmood will announce stronger guidance on police impartiality.
articles.body:
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood is to announce stronger guidance on police impartiality to tackle what she calls the "corrosive and growing perception of two-tier policing".

She will tell a conference of police chiefs that they should avoid what she calls "misguided attempts at course correction" where the pursuit of equality leads instead to differential treatment.

Recent complaints about alleged two-tier policing have mostly come from those on the right in politics.

They have pointed to the arrest of Henry Nowak as he was dying after being stabbed by Vickrum Digwa who had accused him of racism.

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage has argued that white people are treated differently by police because of their race. But critics say this claim risks overlooking the long‑standing experiences of black and minority ethnic communities.

Some senior police figures have also strongly rejected the claim of two-tier policing.

Mahmood will announce a new national standard is being developed "to ensure all members of the public are treated equally", said the Home Office.

"Now let me be clear: I know the vast majority of officers police impartially and that policing without fear or favour is their creed," she will say.

But Mahmood will announce "clear, comprehensive guidance" on police impartiality, which reinforces that officers must apply the law consistently to avoid what she called "motivated actors" whipping up the idea that there's two-tier policing.

Mahmood will say that community engagement can mean going to a residents' association meeting and having tea and biscuits - or samosas - but it shouldn't mean engaging with activists pushing an agenda.

"Leave the politics to the politicians," she will say. "And we will leave the policing to you."

The home secretary will add that more needs to be done to tackle inequalities in policing, highlighting the persistently low proportion of black police officers.

However, she will state that some "well-intentioned approaches", such as the Police Anti-Racism Commitment, "have risked undermining confidence in impartial policing".

"As a Muslim home secretary, no one can doubt that equality in policing, and in our forces, matters to me," she will say.

"But we must also be wary of misguided attempts at course correction, where the pursuit of equality leads instead to differential treatment.

"To the public, it was patently absurd to tell police officers that fair policing "does not mean treating everyone the same."

Jo Noakes who leads the College of Policing, the standards-setting body for the police, said it will issue new guidance for officers that will make clear on impartiality in Spring.

She said: "Policing must act in a way that maintains public confidence, which is dependent on officers and staff exercising their powers without fear or favour...

"Impartiality cannot be seen in isolation but needs to be considered alongside how policing acts with fairness and inclusion - both in its own ranks and with the public."

articles.title: Trump is about to see up close why US efforts won’t stop China’s rise as tech powerhouse
articles.summary: For Xi Jinping, a summit in the high-tech hub of Shenzhen this week is an opportune moment to showcase a vision of China’s unrelenting rise.
articles.body: For Xi Jinping, a summit in the high-tech hub of Shenzhen this week is an opportune moment to showcase a vision of China’s unrelenting rise. Xi is hosting business moguls and world leaders for an annual regional economic summit, where he’ll sit down to sideline talks with US President Donald Trump and hold a three-way meeting with Trump and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, a first-ever trilateral for the nuclear-armed powers. And for his backdrop, Xi has chosen a host city that’s synonymous with China’s rapid transformation into a high-tech powerhouse – and its resilience in the face of US tech and trade frictions. A sprawling metropolis of 18 million, Shenzhen is home to a who’s-who of Chinese tech titans: hardware giant Huawei, dronemaker DJI and the Tesla-beating electric vehicle seller BYD – all companies that have thrived despite US import bans or blacklists. Once known as the capital of luxury knockoffs and cheap electronics, today the city’s high-tech products have helped propel China’s export juggernaut to a record $1 trillion trade surplus already this year. Visiting VIPs who step out onto Shenzhen’s streets this week will find traffic that moves to the whir of homegrown electric vehicles and novelty kiosks where robots serve up coffee. Self-driving taxis ferry passengers and drones deliver take-out in some areas. Surveillance cameras are ubiquitous. The high-tech vision may make for a sharp contrast to the US, where news this week has been dominated by a series of systems outages and a revelation that up until a few months ago the country’s aviation administration was still using floppy disks. For Beijing, the choice of setting is a clear signal to the world of its confidence in the country’s momentum at a moment of intense tech competition with the US. Those optics only came into sharper focus in recent days, as a scandal engulfing American AI chipmaker Nvidia triggered fresh calls to limit China’s access to high-end American technology – a developing situation that could upend a period of relative stability between the two economies. The US Commerce Department earlier this week fired the first shot, unveiling a new rule meant to close loopholes that had allowed Chinese companies to access advanced American chips overseas. Beijing called the move an “abuse of export control measures” and “unjustifiable suppression.” Tech rivalry Even before the latest escalation, pushing back against a US that has increasingly looked to limit Chinese access to key technologies – and dissuade other countries from using China’s – was already baked into Xi’s narrative for Shenzhen. The Chinese leader is taking his turn hosting the annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, a group of nearly two dozen economies from both sides of the Pacific. Members include Southeast Asian nations, Mexico, Canada, Australia and Japan. And Xi hopes that he may find a sympathetic audience among a group of nations that too have been buffeted by US tariffs and global fuel price shocks driven by Trump administration policies, including the war with Iran. Speaking to business leaders in his opening address at the summit on Wednesday, Xi framed China as a defender of globalized trade, calling for countries to reject “unilateralism and protectionism” and keep supply chains open. He also called for deeper AI cooperation – part of the leader’s ongoing bid to pitch China as the leader of a global AI order shaped around a view that the technology should be treated as a “public good.” It’s a conscious contrast to a message from US officials, who will join the summit in China fresh from meeting with allies in Manila, where they likely touted their Pax Silica initiative. That plan aims to get countries to agree to keep China out of sensitive AI supply chains. Xi’s message is an urgent one for Beijing to sell. China’s economy is heavily reliant on its massive, and increasingly high-tech, export engine – and it’s wary of countries around the world throwing up barriers to protect domestic industries from those goods. “Beijing wants these participants to leave believing that engagement with China remains essential to their prosperity,” said Han Lin, who leads China operations for The Asia Group consultancy in Shanghai. For China, the summit “is an opportunity to demonstrate that it remains central to Asia’s economic future.” Global heavyweights But attention from Xi’s main show may be stolen by diplomacy on the summit sidelines, where the Chinese leader’s meetings with Trump and Putin will be another choreographed case in point for China’s growing global heft. Beijing has historically seen meetings with an American president as a way to signal China’s international clout both to its domestic and international audiences. Now, Xi will be hosting what is his third face-to-face meeting with Trump already this year. And even in a historic meeting with Trump and Putin, it’s Xi who appears to be joining the three-way talks in a position of power. Trump is fresh off a bruising defeat in US midterm elections – and entering the backend of his final presidential term. Putin is on what is now a rare international visit after the war in Ukraine made him a global pariah – and sunk his economy. Xi, meanwhile, is expected to cement a fourth term atop China’s authoritarian system at a Communist Party conclave next fall. The trilateral meeting, which Beijing has called “groundbreaking” and said will be a chance to discuss “major issues concerning global peace,” may ultimately yield few tangible outcomes. Xi and Trump, who could meet a further time this year, are expected to use their bilateral this week as a touchstone in ongoing trade negotiations, rather than a moment for hefty breakthroughs. But for Xi, those optics – of high-powered diplomacy before a backdrop calibrated to showcase China’s technological rise – may be outcome enough. articles.title: Trump steps onto global stage weakened at home
articles.summary: President Trump is stepping onto the global stage politically weakened by the sweeping Republican losses in the midterm elections, largely seen as a referendum on Trump himself. Trump is meeting with Indo-Pacific allies at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) this week, before heading to China for an unprecedented trilateral summit with the country’s…
articles.body:
President Trump is stepping onto the global stage politically weakened by the sweeping Republican losses in the midterm elections, largely seen as a referendum on Trump himself.

Trump is meeting with Indo-Pacific allies at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) this week, before heading to China for an unprecedented trilateral summit with the country’s leader, Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

“Even before the midterm elections, many observers at home and abroad already regarded the president as being weaker abroad because of the fallout from the Iran war, because of the continuation of the Russia-Ukraine war,” said Ali Wyne, a senior research and advocacy adviser on U.S.-China relations at the International Crisis Group.

“Now he’s perceived, I think appropriately, as being diminished at home as well,” he continued.

The trip marks Trump’s first outside of the U.S. since Republicans lost control of the House and Senate, dealing a blow to Trump’s ability to push his policy agenda through his final two years in office.

“I’m always amazed at how closely foreign leaders follow our midterm elections, and I think they know what that means,” said Marc Short, Trump’s former legislative director during his first administration.

“But at the same time, it’s President Trump,” he continued. “It’s relative because they know that President Trump is going to be taking a position of maximalist discretion on foreign policy as chief executive officer.”

The president has largely skirted Congress when it comes to foreign policy, even with GOP majorities the past two years.

Trump ordered strikes on Venezuela earlier this year in a successful effort to oust the country’s former President Nicolás Maduro without official approval from Congress.

And his ongoing war on Iran has been carried out without official authorization from Congress, which led to backlash from Democrats and some Republicans.

“He’s operated on his own counsel,” said Cale Brown, a former State Department principal deputy spokesperson in the first Trump administration and chair of Polaris National Security. “He’s never been one to sort of stick his finger in the air and say, ‘Well, which way is Congress feeling,’ before he acts.”

Brown argued that Trump could be emboldened going into Thursday’s meetings.

“These relationships have always been very personal ones for the president,” Brown said, referring to his relationships with foreign leaders, including Xi and Putin.

“You could argue that with the midterms behind him, he is in many ways liberated,” he said.

Trump will participate in a bilateral meeting with Xi on Wednesday. Xi hosted Trump for a state visit in Beijing in May, while Trump hosted Xi at the White House in September. The two leaders are also slated to meet at the Group of 20 summit in Miami next month.

On Thursday, Trump and Xi will be joined by Putin for a trilateral summit. Trump has signaled he would like to talk about the U.S. war in Iran, the Russia-Ukraine War and denuclearization.

All three issues have been foreign policy priorities for Trump during his second term, but Xi and Putin have shown little interest in compromise.

Washington has largely supported Ukraine in its effort to prevent Russia from taking over the country, while China has helped support Russia. Meanwhile, Iran has received support from Moscow and Beijing in its war against the U.S.

On nuclear nonproliferation, China has resisted any checks on its buildup of nuclear weapons.

“We have three people going into the same meeting, but they’re not talking about the same agenda,” said Steve Yates, former deputy national security adviser to former Vice President Dick Cheney and senior research fellow at the Heritage Foundation.

“I think that’s fair for a first meeting. I wouldn’t expect this to be a world-changing declaration,” he continued. “And I don’t think the midterms change that for either Xi or Putin.”

Trump is also not the first president to take part in foreign negotiations around the time of an election shellacking. Former President Carter normalized relations with China during the Iran hostage crisis, which contributed to his nearly 10-point loss to former President Reagan in the 1980 presidential election.

“These other countries, and their leaderships, and their one-party states have long memories, and they’re not really moved by the biorhythms that we get caught up in,” Yates said. “In my experience, none of this moves the needle for them.”

Michael O’Hanlon, director of research in the Brookings Institution’s Foreign Policy program, argued the president’s clout should not be underestimated.

“It’s not like they are underestimating an American president’s power because he doesn’t control Congress the way he used to,” O’Hanlon said. “American presidents are still leading the most powerful military and economy on earth.”

Regardless of the outcome of the meeting, strategists and analysts predict Trump will likely tout the summit as progress.

“As he’s more constrained at home, more concerned with shoring up his legacy, more hopeful that he can leave office with some dramatic, headline grabbing accomplishments, I suspect he will be more receptive to taking steps that might not be advantageous from the perspective of the U.S. national security interests, but could at least allow him to say he was able to achieve what none of his predecessors could,” Wyne said.

Others note that Xi and Putin realize they may never deal with a president like Trump again, and view these dynamics as conducive to beneficial deals.

“Maybe it’s that they would both see this as an opportunity for them,” Short said.

Trump wouldn’t be the first president to intensify his focus on foreign policy during his final years in office.

“It’s always the part of their portfolio where they have a little bit more direct control, but it’s not as if he [Trump] can just ignore the domestic side of things. We still have budgets to pass, Social Security to deal with, AI regulation, golden dome missile defense,” O’Hanlon said.

“It’s now going to be more contested,” he added. “He no longer has a Republican Congress rubber-stamping his every whim the way he did last year in particular.”

articles.title: Waymo pauses all US freeway operations of its self-driving cars after California ban
articles.summary: Waymo is temporarily pausing driverless rides on freeways in all its markets after California’s Department of Motor Vehicles said Tuesday that its self-drivi...
articles.body:
Waymo is temporarily pausing driverless rides on freeways in all its markets after California's Department of Motor Vehicles said Tuesday that its self-driving vehicles can't use state freeways for now, citing safety concerns following a series of incidents.

Waymo has allowed its cars to operate on freeways in five of its 13 operating areas across the US: San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles County, Phoenix, Miami and Austin, according to the company.

California's DMV said the autonomous cars pose "imminent hazard to public safety" following at least two recent incidents involving the vehicles. In one occasion, three Waymo vehicles entered an active construction zone along US Route 101, while another incident involved California Highway Patrol vehicles on Highway 280, the department said.

In the latter, a Waymo vehicle attempted to pass patrol cars conducting a traffic break earlier this month, CNN affiliate KGO reported.

According to the agency, Waymo vehicles have made "recurrent incursions" into active construction zones, putting workers, other vehicles and equipment at risk.

"We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations," a Waymo spokesperson said.

The company noted the US Route 101 incident did not result in any injuries or collisions.

This is the second time this year Waymo has faced highway restrictions in the state, according to CNN affiliate KGO . The company paused freeway operations in May in San Francisco and Los Angeles to improve its vehicles' response to construction zones. The previous restriction followed similar incidents that month, according to the California DMV.

A CNN analysis in June found hundreds of incidents in which robotaxis allegedly made dangerous maneuvers and struggled with obstacles that humans instinctively handle. They ran red lights, drove into oncoming traffic and active crime scenes, failed to abide by emergency road closures and came within inches of pedestrians lawfully crossing the street.

On Tuesday, a Waymo spokesperson pointed to the company's June statement in response to CNN reporting. Waymo said it took public feedback seriously and is actively working on improvements for some of the issues raised, but that these were largely isolated incidents. The overwhelming majority of rides are smooth and uneventful, the company said.

Waymo data said its vehicles are involved in 95% fewer crashes resulting in serious injuries, or worse, than human drivers.

The restriction went into effect on November 11 and will remain in effect until Waymo addresses the safety lapses, the California DMV said.

articles.title: Police to reinvestigate case against man charged in Tasia Fortune’s killing
articles.summary: JACKSON, Miss. — The murder case against a man charged after a Black woman was found hanged in a Jackson, Mississippi, tree has been sent back to police detectives for additional investigation.
articles.body: JACKSON, Miss. — The murder case against a man charged after a Black woman was found hanged in a Jackson, Mississippi, tree has been sent back to police detectives for additional investigation. A judge agreed Tuesday during Earnest Lloyd Jr.’s preliminary hearing that there was not enough evidence against him to proceed. WAPT-TV reports that prosecutors said the case was not ready to go before a grand jury. Lloyd, 25, is one of three men charged in the death of 29-year-old Tasia Fortune. Fortune’s body was found Aug. 3 in a tree behind a vacant house. Her death stoked fears that Fortune was targeted because of her race and conjured memories of the state’s long and painful history of lynching. However, all three suspects in Fortune’s death are Black. Authorities say that the three staged the scene after a drug dispute. The Associated Press sent emails Tuesday seeking comment from the Hinds County District Attorney’s office and the attorney listed as representing Lloyd. State Public Defender Andre de Gruy said his office is not representing Lloyd but that he believes if the evidence at a preliminary hearing is insufficient, then the case should be dismissed “without prejudice.” He added that Lloyd should be released from custody, that an investigation could continue and charges could be refiled at a later date. Lloyd did not appear in court Tuesday. He was in transit from a jail in northern Mississippi, and the hearing took place without him. Tommie Brown, public information officer for the Jackson Police Department, had no comment Tuesday afternoon on the decision to send the case back for further investigation. Lloyd had been held at the Tallahatchie Correctional Facility but was to be moved to the Hinds County Detention Center, according to WAPT-TV. Some officials had called for a federal civil rights investigation into Fortune’s killing, but Police Chief RaShall Brackney said that props were left at the scene “as part of the staging” of Fortune’s death. Over the past two years, about a half-dozen Black women and men have been found hanged across the South. None of the deaths has been found to be criminal, though in some cases critics said that law enforcement appeared to move quickly to label them suicides before having sufficient evidence to rule out foul play. Like Lloyd, 45-year-old Eric Clark and 51-year-old Jarques Ratliff are being held on murder charges. Police have said that Ratliff had an “association” with Fortune. Judge Jeffery Reynolds, who set bond at $5 million for Clark following his arrest in late September, called Fortune’s killing “heinous.” “People justifiably didn’t know if we had a killer on the loose who might hang people for racial reasons,” Reynolds said. Brackney said that the fear that the image of Fortune’s hanging body evoked has damaged the community. “We know we have a very sordid history around lynchings and racial terror across this nation and particularly around the South. That is still a very current narrative. It is still a very raw narrative,” she said. Prior to any of the arrests, Fortune’s mother, Christy Spivey, told The Associated Press that she didn’t believe race had anything to do with her daughter’s death. Spivey is white. She said that Fortune’s father is Black. “I think this is something very personal, very personal,” Spivey said, insisting that someone who was acquainted with Fortune was involved. Spivey said that following a hearing for Ratliff earlier in September, Clark hugged her at the courthouse. “He never said he did it, but he said he was there to turn himself in for murder,” Spivey told reporters following Clark’s own hearing later that month.

articles.title: Aluno se emociona com evolução no Saresp em Altinópolis (SP) | G1
articles.standfirst: Após apresentar resultado insatisfatório em primeiro simulado, Eduardo, de 10 anos, teve o maior avanço entre 200 estudantes do 5º ano de escola municipal.
articles.summary: Eduardo Delfino, de 10 anos, viralizou ao receber medalha pela maior evolução no simulado do Saresp após superar dificuldades em escola de Altinópolis.
articles.body:
O choro sincero de um estudante de 10 anos ganhou as redes sociais na última semana quando o aluno foi homenageado diante de outros colegas em Altinópolis (SP).

No vídeo, Eduardo Delfino aparece abraçado por um amigo e emocionado, ao ouvir a professora, também comovida, anunciar que ele tinha atingido a maior evolução nos preparativos para o Sistema de Avaliação de Rendimento Escolar do Estado (Saresp) entre os 200 alunos do quinto ano da Escola Municipal Ana Lúcia Felipe Penteado Ferreira.

Um feito obtido depois de muito reforço após um resultado insuficiente em um primeiro simulado.

"Eu me sinto feliz, muito feliz mesmo, por ter aprendido muito", conta o estudante.

A escola no bairro Figueiredo Walter tem 300 alunos, entre eles 200 do quinto ano do ensino fundamental que estão prestes a fazer a prova do Saresp, aplicada pelo Estado anualmente para diagnosticar a qualidade da educação básica paulista.

Como parte do treinamento, os alunos fizeram simulados ao longo do ano. No primeiro deles, Eduardo lembra que não foi bem e que ficou chateado com o desempenho.

Eduardo, de 10 anos, se emocionou com premiação por desempenho nos estudos para o Saresp em Altinópolis (SP). — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

"A minha dificuldade era mais na língua portuguesa, porque na língua portuguesa estavam as perguntas mais complicadas", conta.

Com Eduardo e outros alunos, a professora Juliana Prodóssimo intensificou os estudos ao longo dos meses, com aulas no contraturno e outras estratégias de aprendizagem.

O trabalho surtiu efeito. No último simulado, Eduardo não só saiu do patamar considerado insuficiente, como foi para o nível máximo e melhorou o resultado em 44%, a maior evolução entre os colegas, que também se destacaram em toda a rede de ensino de Altinópolis.

"Para estar dando esse suporte na escola, que é onde a gente diagnostica as defasagens e as dificuldades, essa equipe de professores faz as estratégias de que forma que a gente vai buscar naquele aluno que está faltando nele", diz.

Eduardo, de 10 anos, em escola municipal de Altinópolis (SP). — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Com o resultado positivo de Eduardo e da turma em geral, a escola preparou uma cerimônia no pátio para divulgar a conquista na última sexta-feira (13).

Diante de todos os alunos reunidos, Eduardo ouviu emocionado a sua trajetória de estudos pelas palavras da professora Juliana. Além da medalha, recebeu demonstrações de carinho e abraços de colegas e docentes.

"Não fui eu que ganhei, mas eu me senti feliz pela outra pessoa que ganhou. Isso é sempre importante na vida dos outros", conta o colega Brayan Henrique de Souza, o primeiro a abraçar Eduardo na cerimônia.

Em casa, Eduardo é motivo de orgulho da família. Segundo a mãe, Fabíola Carolina Delfino, o filho não teve apenas uma nota excelente no simulado, como melhorou em todas as disciplinas.

"Eu sabia que ele estava evoluindo, eu vim acompanhando a evolução dele, mas não imaginei que ele ia ser em primeiro lugar, ficar em primeiro lugar", diz.

Estudantes de Altinópolis (SP) tiveram reforço nos estudos para melhorar preparação para o Saresp. — Foto: Reprodução/ EPTV

O fim de semana em Belo Horizonte e na Região Metropolitana está com atrações para todos os gostos. O g1 preparou uma agenda cultural com opções para aproveitar. Confira:

Jão em sessão de fotos do disco 'Memórias Póstumas' — Foto: Divulgação/Hugo Comte

Jão desembarca em Belo Horizonte neste sábado (21) com a turnê “ Memórias Póstumas ”. O cantor se apresenta no Mineirinho, em um dos grandes shows da programação cultural da cidade neste fim de semana. A turnê aposta em uma produção que mistura música, teatro e elementos visuais, com uma narrativa dividida em atos e referências a temas como memória, ausência e passagem do tempo.

Entre os elementos do espetáculo estão palco 360°, corpo de balé e intervenções teatrais da atriz Isabel Teixeira, que interpreta a Morte e conduz monólogos ao longo da apresentação. Os ingressos podem ser comprados neste link .

🕗 Horário: 21h; abertura dos portões às 18h

🏠 Local: Mineirinho - Av. Antônio Abrahão Caram, 1000

Zé Ramalho é segunda atração a subir no palco principal do Festival de Inverno Bahia 2026. — Foto: Laecio Lacerda

Zé Ramalho se apresenta em Belo Horizonte nesta sexta-feira (20), em BH. Aos 77 anos, o cantor e compositor traz à capital mineira o “Show dos Sucessos”, com repertório dedicado a músicas que marcaram sua carreira.

O público poderá ouvir canções como “Avôhai”, “Chão de Giz”, “Frevo Mulher”, “Admirável Gado Novo”, “Sinônimos” e “Beira-Mar”. Ingressos entre R$ 180,00 e R$ 520,00 e podem ser comprados aqui.

🏠 Local: Arena Hall - Av. Nossa Senhora do Carmo, 230.

Espetáculo “São Francisco de Assis à Foz” será apresentado no Teatro Feluma, em BH — Foto: Guto Muniz - Divulgação

O premiado espetáculo “ São Francisco de Assis à Foz ” retorna a Belo Horizonte. A montagem aproxima duas trajetórias: a de Francisco de Assis, que abre mão dos próprios bens para servir aos pobres, e a do Rio São Francisco em seu percurso pelo sertão até a foz.

Com Glicério Rosário em cena, o espetáculo mistura referências religiosas, sociais e ambientais e propõe uma reflexão sobre desigualdade, afeto e os impactos da transposição do Velho Chico. A peça recebeu três prêmios Sesc-Sated em 2009: Melhor Espetáculo, Melhor Direção e Melhor Ator.

🏠 Local: Teatro Feluma - Alameda Ezequiel Dias, 275, Centro.

Festival reúne gastronomia e produtos derivados da jabuticaba em Sabará. — Foto: Reprodução / Prefeitura de Sabará (MG)

O Festival da Jabuticaba de Sabará comemora 40 anos com quatro dias de programação, reunindo gastronomia, música, artesanato e produtos feitos com a fruta. Com entrada gratuita, o evento terá 30 estandes de derivados da jabuticaba, como geleias, molhos e licores, além de 16 espaços gastronômicos.

Entre os destaques está a Cozinha Show, com chefs convidados preparando receitas doces e salgadas à base da fruta. Na abertura, na quinta-feira, um bolo de jabuticaba especialmente preparado para os 40 anos vai homenagear a Praça Santa Rita , onde ocorreu a primeira edição do festival. A programação inclui ainda apresentações musicais de artistas locais e atividades culturais e turísticas. A entrada é gratuita e não precisa de ingresso.

📅 Data: de 19 a 22 de novembro - quinta a domingo

Espetáculo “Flashback – As Vozes do Mundo” celebra clássicos da música internacional em BH. — Foto: Divulgação

Sucessos que marcaram as décadas de 1960 a 1990 embalam o espetáculo “ Flashback – As Vozes do Mundo ”, em Belo Horizonte. Com banda ao vivo, o show reúne clássicos do pop, rock, disco, soul e da música romântica, passando por nomes como Elvis Presley, Michael Jackson, Whitney Houston, Madonna, Bee Gees, ABBA, Prince, Cyndi Lauper e Tina Turner.

O repertório inclui ainda músicas de Earth, Wind & Fire, Boney M, Barbra Streisand, Erasure, Tears for Fears e Kool & The Gang, além de canções que ficaram conhecidas nas trilhas de filmes como Grease e Dirty Dancing. Ingressos podem ser comprados neste link.

articles.title: ‘Human’ revealed as Cambridge Dictionary Word of the Year for 2026
articles.summary: Amid the global debate surrounding artificial intelligence, Cambridge Dictionary has named “human” as its Word of the Year for 2026.
articles.body: Amid the global debate surrounding artificial intelligence, Cambridge Dictionary has named “human” as its Word of the Year for 2026. In a statement published Wednesday, Cambridge Dictionary said that human is defined in the Cambridge Dictionary as “having the qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines.” Explaining its choice, the dictionary said that this year has been “defined by global debates on what it means to be human when AI is blurring the boundaries between people and machines.” It cited public interventions by intellectuals such as AI pioneer and Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton, who said: “We’re creating alien beings. I’m willing to be selfish and choose humans.” Cambridge Dictionary highlighted the advance of AI deepfakes that can simulate humans, and the reaction to this technology from celebrities such as Matthew McConaughey and Taylor Swift, who have trademarked images of themselves as well as clips of their voices. Lexicographer Colin McIntosh of the Cambridge Dictionary added that “AI is changing how we talk about being human.” “The definition of ‘human’ has traditionally distinguished us from gods, animals, and, latterly, from machines,” he said in the statement. “A recent increase in compounds such as ‘human-made’ highlight how the word has come to distinguish works or qualities of people, as distinct from AI,” added McIntosh. “It’s this renewed interest in the idea of being human that captured the zeitgeist.” In addition to choosing its Word of the Year, Cambridge Dictionary also revealed a number of new words and phrases that it has added this year. The first is “air jail,” defined as “a method of trying to train an animal, especially a dog, that involves holding them off the ground for a period of time when they show aggressive or other unwanted behaviour.” Another is “aura farming,” which it says is “the activity of doing things with the intention of showing a personality that people admire and think is attractive and interesting.” The dictionary also now includes “looksmaxxing,” defined as “the activity of making yourself as physically attractive as possible, as encouraged by some people, mainly young men, on social media.”

articles.title: DR Congo’s rival peace efforts fail to halt violence in the east
articles.summary: Diplomatic efforts struggle to end fighting in eastern DRC as civilians continue to bear the cost of conflict.
articles.body:
Bukavu, DRC – For residents of eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), the succession of diplomatic initiatives meant to end years of conflict is becoming increasingly difficult to reconcile with the violence unfolding around them.

In North and South Kivu provinces, fighting between the Congolese army and the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), an armed and political coalition led by former President Joseph Kabila, has continued despite international efforts to secure a settlement. Civilians remain exposed to attacks, displacement and the disruption of essential services.

The latest escalation has raised questions about whether negotiations in Washington and Doha can deliver security on the ground, and whether the separate diplomatic efforts are sufficiently coordinated to make progress.

“One meeting follows another, and they all end up being much the same,” said Blaise Chasumba, a resident of Bukavu, the provincial capital of South Kivu. “But the real peace that the warring parties are dangling before us is far from becoming a reality on the ground. We continue to lose our loved ones and our homes.”

The Washington Accords, signed in December 2025, seek to address tensions between the DRC and neighbouring Rwanda. The Doha process, by contrast, is intended to resolve the conflict between the Congolese government and the Congo River Alliance (AFC), which includes the Rwanda-backed M23 armed group.

The distinction is important: an agreement between Kinshasa and Kigali cannot, on its own, resolve the confrontation between the Congolese government and armed groups operating inside the country.

The Doha Framework for a Comprehensive Peace Agreement was signed by the DRC government, the AFC and M23 on November 15, 2025. In August 2026, representatives of the two sides, alongside Qatar, the United States, Togo, the African Union Commission and Switzerland, agreed on a road map to advance negotiations and establish a mechanism to review implementation. Fighting has nevertheless continued.

The roots of the conflict stretch back decades. The 1994 genocide in neighbouring Rwanda and the flight of former Rwandan soldiers and militia members into what was then Zaire helped create the conditions for successive wars. The presence of armed groups linked to the genocide, and the emergence of the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR), became a persistent source of tension between Kinshasa and Kigali.

The First and Second Congo Wars, which began in 1996 and 1998, drew in several neighbouring countries. Although the conflicts formally ended, disputes over land, political representation, citizenship and control of natural resources continued to drive violence in the east.

M23 emerged in 2012 after a mutiny by former members of the National Congress for the Defence of the People (CNDP). The group had been integrated into the Congolese army under a March 23, 2009 peace agreement, which its leaders later accused the government of failing to honour. The United Nations and conflict researchers have documented the movement’s origins in the breakdown of that integration process.

The diplomatic landscape has since become more complicated. Established in October 2026 under Kabila’s leadership, the FRN says it has succeeded the AFC and assumed its commitments. The precise relationship between the new coalition and the earlier AFC/M23 structure remains important when assessing who is represented in the negotiations.

On the battlefield, an offensive in early November underlined the fragility of the diplomatic process. FRN fighters advanced through Kahuzi-Biega National Park and along National Road 3, a strategic route linking Bukavu with areas farther north.

Conflict monitoring reports said the fighters captured several localities, including Bitale and the centre of Bulambika on November 8 . The Congolese army said it had halted the advance at Bulambika and was preparing a counteroffensive. Local and military accounts differed over the extent of the fighters’ territorial gains.

Diplomatic commitments, limited progress

The fighting has driven further displacement and placed additional pressure on communities already struggling with years of conflict. Humanitarian organisations have warned that conflict is also making it harder to maintain essential services.

Doctors Without Borders, known by its French initials MSF, said it had reduced its staff presence in the Bunyakiri health zone, relocating some personnel to Bitale and Bukavu as the security situation deteriorated.

“We remind all parties to the conflict of the importance and the obligation to respect and ensure the protection of healthcare facilities, civilian populations and humanitarian staff, in accordance with international humanitarian law,” MSF said in a statement sent to Al Jazeera.

The Congolese armed forces, known by their French acronym FARDC, have blamed recent attacks in North and South Kivu on the Rwandan army and fighters allied with the FRN. The army says it is preparing operations to recover lost positions.

Rwanda denies supporting armed groups in eastern DRC, citing the presence of the FDLR as a security threat. The dispute has remained central to tensions between the two countries.

In a resolution adopted in February 2025, the UN Security Council condemned M23’s offensive and described direct support and participation by the Rwanda Defence Force. It called on Rwanda to end its support and withdraw its forces from Congolese territory. The resolution also condemned support provided by Congolese forces to armed groups, particularly the FDLR, and called for the group’s neutralisation.

The African Union (AU) has acknowledged the gap between diplomatic commitments and conditions on the ground. In a communique issued after a Peace and Security Council meeting on October 26 , it said implementation of commitments under the Washington and Doha processes remained limited. It called for better coordination between the initiatives and urged inclusive, nationally owned dialogue.

The AU’s assessment points to a central weakness in the peace efforts: Agreements and diplomatic meetings have not translated into a sustained improvement in security. The bloc has stressed that a lasting settlement requires political dialogue involving wider sections of Congolese society, including women, young people and civil society organisations.

Civilians demand a voice in the peace process

For some Congolese, negotiations between governments and armed groups are not enough. They want a broader political process that addresses the grievances sustaining the conflict.

Dieumerci Mungu Akonkwa, North Kivu coordinator for Action for Democracy and Development in the Congo, said the negotiations had yet to produce tangible improvements for civilians.

“Since these negotiations began on the ground, there has been no progress. All that is happening is that the lives of peaceful civilians are being cut short. The war continues to create displaced people, and women are being raped,” he said.

Akonkwa called for an inclusive national dialogue, pointing to proposals put forward by Catholic and Protestant church leaders. Such a process, he argued, could bring political actors and civil society into discussions that extend beyond negotiations between the government and armed groups.

The challenge is not only to secure commitments from the parties to the conflict, but to address the local disputes, weak state institutions and impunity that have helped sustain violence in eastern DRC. Without progress on those issues, a political agreement risks leaving the underlying causes of insecurity unresolved.

For residents, however, the immediate measure of progress is simpler: whether the fighting stops, essential services remain available and families can return home.

Chasumba said people were also waiting for those responsible for the destruction to address their losses.

“We are eager to see compensation for the damage caused by the war. Unfortunately, at this rate, we can see that we are in for a long-running saga, full of twists and turns,” he said.

articles.title: Kim Jong Un's daughter hits ski slopes in rare photos as North Korean dictator tours mountain resort
articles.summary: Kim Jong Un watched from a throne-like chair, cigarette in hand, as his daughter Kim Ju Ae skied down a snowy North Korean resort during a family outing.
articles.body: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un was photographed sitting in an ornate, throne-like armchair in the middle of a snowy ski resort while his daughter, viewed as his likely successor, carved down the slopes during an unusual family outing. The striking images, released Monday by North Korean state media, show Kim wearing sunglasses and dress shoes while seated in the elaborate upholstered chair, holding a lit cigarette.Other photographs show his daughter skiing in an all-white outfit as officials navigate the slopes nearby. The girl, believed to be named Kim Ju Ae, has increasingly appeared alongside her father at high-profile public events. South Korea's National Intelligence Service has assessed that she is being positioned as his likely successor, although North Korea has not publicly confirmed a succession plan. TRUMP ARRIVES IN PHILIPPINES AHEAD OF XI JINPING SUMMIT IN CHINA AFTER GOP MIDTERM LOSSES The snowy spectacle unfolded just as President Donald Trump raised the possibility that Kim could make an unexpected appearance during his upcoming high-stakes meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. "We might have Kim Jong Un. He may come, I don't know. That's up to President Xi," Trump told reporters Monday. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump was serious about potentially meeting Kim, though no talks were confirmed. "If we have a problem with North Korea, the only way we're ever going to solve it is if we engage with them," Rubio told reporters in the Philippines, adding that a meeting "may not happen." TRUMP’S ASIA TRIP TAKES ALASKA DETOUR AS WEATHER FORCES REFUELING STOP CHANGE The photographs were taken during Kim's Nov. 15–16 inspection of a tourist zone under development in Samjiyon, a mountainous city in northern North Korea, according to a report by the state-run Pyongyang Times reviewed by Fox News Digital. Kim visited a ski resort under construction near Mount Pukphothae, where he examined skiing tracks and equipment and instructed officials to prepare the facilities for operation, the outlet reported. His daughter was photographed skiing at the tourist zone on Nov. 15, according to an Associated Press caption accompanying the government-provided images. The North Korean leader's visit was part of a broader effort to transform Samjiyon into a year-round mountain tourism destination, with plans for hotels, ski facilities, railway connections and an expanded airport. TRUMP PLAYS NUCLEAR POKER WITH KIM JONG UN — BUT WHO HOLDS THE CARDS? The appearance of Kim's daughter added another layer of intrigue to the ski resort visit. South Korean intelligence officials have pointed to her increasingly prominent public role as evidence that she may eventually inherit power from her father. In an October 2026, assessment reported by KBS World, the National Intelligence Service said her position as a potential successor was strengthening. The agency has also noted her frequent appearances at military-related events, although the North Korean government has made no formal announcement identifying her as the country's next leader. The latest photographs offered a different setting for the young girl, showing her navigating a groomed ski slope rather than accompanying her father at an official event. Meanwhile, the possibility of renewed diplomacy between Trump and Kim remains uncertain. Trump and Kim last met in 2019, when their summit in Hanoi ended without an agreement on North Korea's nuclear program. Efforts to restart negotiations have since stalled as Pyongyang has continued developing its nuclear and missile capabilities. articles.title: Board of Peace warns Gaza ceasefire faces imminent collapse without action
articles.summary: The US-led board has decried continued fighting in Gaza and delays in implementing the terms of a 2025 ceasefire deal.
articles.body:
The United States-backed Board of Peace has delivered a grim assessment to the United Nations Security Council, warning diplomats of conditions that threaten the year-old truce in war-torn Gaza.

In its latest report, submitted on Tuesday, the board cautioned that, without immediate steps to implement the 2025 ceasefire deal, the truce between Israel and Hamas may be on the brink of collapse.

“The distance between what has been agreed and what is happening on the ground nonetheless remains the principal risk to the process,” the report said, which The Associated Press obtained.

The Board of Peace was created in 2025, at US President Donald Trump’s behest, to oversee the ceasefire deal and reconstruction in Gaza.

Since October 2023, the narrow coastal territory has been the target of a genocidal war carried out by Israel, which has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians.

In recent weeks, Israel has continued to carry out deadly air strikes, and its ongoing restrictions have prevented the delivery of life-saving aid into Gaza ahead of the winter season.

“Restrictions imposed by Israel on the entry of supplies and equipment, compounded by funding shortfalls, continued to impede preparedness and response efforts,” the board said in its report.

According to the board, the widespread devastation in Gaza has left Palestinians facing “another winter in tents and rubble”.

Trump first proposed the Board of Peace in September 2025, saying it would stabilise Gaza and ensure lasting peace.

The board’s mission was laid out in a 20-point Gaza peace plan , as well as the ceasefire between Israel and Hamas. The ceasefire formally began on October 10, 2025, though attacks have continued since.

The plan envisioned steps for each side to take that could eventually create a “credible pathway” to Palestinian statehood.

But in Tuesday’s report, the board said Israel and Hamas have fallen far short of their commitments in the ceasefire deal.

“A ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely,” the report said. “Should it collapse, there would be no road map to return to, no administration to deploy and no enabling environment to rebuild.”

The board also noted that Israel has blocked the technocratic civil administration body created to run Gaza on an interim basis.

“The absence of decisions by the government of Israel on the necessary conditions and arrangements for the training, deployment and return of civilian police to Gaza continues to impede full implementation of the Comprehensive Plan,” the report said.

“The Board of Peace calls on the government of Israel to take these decisions without delay.”

To break the deadlock, the board called on the UN Security Council to press both sides to fulfil their agreements.

“Neither party may treat the other’s delay as license for its own inaction, and together these obligations are the only route to Israeli withdrawal and reconstruction at scale,” the report said.

It also added that the outcome must establish a credible path towards Palestinian statehood and self-determination, warning that no unilateral actions should be permitted to derail that ultimate goal.

articles.title: Man charged over ‘brutal attack’ on Somali-American in Minnesota
articles.summary: Rideshare driver Mohamed Yusuf is in a critical condition after he was allegedly assaulted by a passenger.
articles.body:
A 25-year-old man has been charged in Minnesota with attempted murder and carjacking after an attack on a Somali-American Uber driver that prosecutors describe as “incredibly brutal”.

Mohamed Yusuf, 51, suffered broken ribs, a broken leg, spinal injuries, collapsed lungs and significant internal bleeding after being strangled with a seatbelt and run over by his own car in the city of Hopkins early on Saturday, according to court documents. His family said he was in a coma.

“It was an incredibly brutal attack,” Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty said on Tuesday.

She said her office had charged Samit Apurva Patel with one count of second-degree attempted murder and one count of first-degree carjacking for the assault on Yusuf on November 14. Patel was taken into custody on Saturday.

Yusuf’s family claimed the attack was driven by hate, while civil rights advocates demanded a hate crime investigation.

Prosecutors said the evidence could not prove beyond a reasonable doubt that Patel’s behaviour was motivated by bias, though that “does not diminish the pain that the family and the Somali community is feeling right now”, Moriarty said.

The court filing said Yusuf was on the phone with his brother, who is also an Uber driver, when Yusuf picked up the passenger just before 1am on Saturday. His brother allegedly heard the passenger tell Yusuf that he did not like the name Mohamed.

“He was apparently pulled out of the car and was standing there when Patel drove over him and might have circled back and driven over him again,” Moriarty said.

Patel’s parents called police for a wellness check after he arrived home appearing intoxicated and “exhibiting signs of emotional distress and belligerent behavior”, according to the court filing.

When the officers arrived, they found Yusuf’s car in the driveway with the exterior and driver’s seatbelt damaged. The phone call with Yusuf’s brother was still active through the car’s system, court records show.

Officers said Patel told them he had been drinking and “admitted he took an Uber home, but he claimed not to know where his Uber driver was”, the filing says.

Officers found Yusuf in a patch of burs in a ditch off the side of the road using location data from his smartwatch and a drone with thermal imaging.

Uber said in a statement that it was horrified by the attack, that it has been in touch with the driver’s family and has banned the rider from the platform.

Rights advocates have raised concerns about rhetoric against Somali Americans by US President Donald Trump and his allies, and condemned his immigration crackdown in Minnesota .

US rights advocates have also noted rising Islamophobia over the past two-plus decades following the September 11, 2001, attacks, and more recently due to anti-immigration policies, rising white supremacy movements and the fallout from Israel’s war on Gaza.

articles.title: Rare images of Indigenous group in Amazon highlight threats, advocates say
articles.summary: Illegal activities in the Amazon pose grave risks to uncontacted Indigenous groups like Brazil’s Awa,.
articles.body:
Rare images of an isolated Indigenous group emerging from a remote part of Brazil’s Amazon rainforest have highlighted the threats they face from loggers, hunters and ranchers, advocates say.

Survival International, a UK-based Indigenous rights group, shared images on Tuesday of a “historic encounter” on Monday in the northeastern state of Maranhao between a government team and about 20 uncontacted Awa people, who asked for food.

The Awa are a Tupi-Guarani people in northwestern Maranhao, some of whom remain in voluntary isolation, according to Funai, Brazil’s Indigenous affairs agency.

Funai told the Reuters news agency it was reviewing videos and accounts on social media showing isolated Awa interacting with a village in the Arariboia Indigenous Land, and that the Brazilian state was not seeking contact with the group, in line with its policy of non-contact.

Brazil’s Ministry of Indigenous Peoples said the encounter began on Monday near a government access control post and the village of Tawari, home to Guajajara Indigenous people, The Associated Press (AP) news agency reported. The footage was recorded by members of the Guajajara community, according to AP.

Survival International said it released the footage at the request of the Guardians of the Amazon, an Indigenous group that campaigns against illegal loggers and ranchers.

“The uncontacted Awa are under extreme pressure as intruders encroach from all sides of their territory, driving them into an ever-smaller island of the Amazon rainforest, surrounded by destruction,” said Caroline Pearce, Survival International’s director.

The Maranhao Indigenous people’s organisation COAPIMA said the encounter showed the need for careful action by the responsible agencies because of the risks that unplanned contact can pose to isolated groups , mainly from exposure to diseases.

In recent decades, isolated Indigenous groups across the Amazon have faced encroaching illegal miners, loggers and ranchers.

Contact with the groups can be deadly. In Colombia, about 40 percent of the isolated Nukak people died from diseases after outsiders reached them in the 1980s.

“If there is no forest, there are no uncontacted peoples,” Teresa Mayo, a senior researcher at Survival International, told Al Jazeera in a report on the Nukak.

articles.title: ‘No imminent threat’: Rubio hits back at Iran dirty bomb report, brands intelligence sources ‘liars’
articles.summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio has dismissed concerns about a possible Iranian plot to target Washington, DC, with a dirty bomb or chemical weapons,
articles.body: US secretary of state Marco Rubio has dismissed concerns about a possible Iranian plot to target Washington, DC, with a dirty bomb or chemical weapons, saying the United States does not face an “imminent threat”. Rubio also accused the intelligence sources cited in media reports of spreading unverified information.Speaking to reporters in the Philippines early Wednesday, Rubio responded to a CNN report alleging that Tehran was developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials in the US capital.Asked whether he was concerned about an imminent attack on Washington, Rubio said, “I am not. But again, we're concerned every day about anything that threatens our country ... I don't think there's any imminent threat.”He added, “The United States is always on the lookout for anyone who tries to do harm to our country and to our people. And we have threat streams every day, and the majority of them are not credible. We have to follow up on them.”Rubio also criticised the intelligence sources cited in the report, saying, “Some of your (media outlets) intelligence sources are liars; others are liars and criminals.”“They're liars because they're making it up. You have liars who are criminals because not only are they making things up – but maybe it's half true. But they are sharing intelligence information the way they shouldn't be,” he added.The secretary of state declined to comment on the specific allegations, saying he did not know who was providing the information to journalists.“That specific report I won't even comment on it because I don't know who's leaking this stuff to you guys,” Rubio said. “They're either showboats and liars, or ... probably criminals if they're saying anything that's even half true,” he added.Reiterating Washington's position on security preparedness, Rubio said the administration remained alert to threats against American citizens and institutions.He also expressed confidence in the country's intelligence capabilities and its ability to identify potential threats before they materialise.“I feel a lot of confidence in our intelligence services. I have a lot of confidence in our systems of being able to identify these things ahead of time,” Rubio said. Defending Washington's vigilance against Tehran and other potential threats, Rubio said, “Let there be no doubt whether it’s the Iranian regime or terrorists around the world who have repeatedly said that they want to harm Americans. The Iranians have been chanting death to America since 1979.”Iran rejects allegationsIranian foreign minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi had earlier rejected the allegations, accusing pro-Israel media of spreading propaganda to build support for a potential conflict with Tehran.In a post on X, Araghchi said: “In the past 72 hours, pro-Israel media have "reported" that Iran is supposedly plotting to use chemical weapons in DC while building missile bases under dams. RUBBISH.“Spare us the Iraq War-style propaganda, especially with Israeli fingerprints all over it. Nobody is buying it.”Additionally, Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf had also dismissed the reports, writing: “Same false flags, same war mongering, new logos. The right’s credibility deficit is maxed out, so the messaging operation pivoted to NYT and CNN.”What the CNN report saidCNN, citing seven US officials, reported that American intelligence had detected Iranian planning for potential attacks against senior Trump administration officials in Washington, DC, involving a dirty bomb or chemical weapons.According to the report, the intelligence indicated that Tehran was exploring options rather than preparing an imminent attack. Two sources said the alleged planning included specific locations and targets, prompting US contingency preparations.White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said the administration was “monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland.”Trump warns Iran of consequencesEarlier, US president Donald Trump warned Tehran of unprecedented consequences if it attempted an attack on American soil.“Well, if there is, they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before,” Trump said, adding, “I hope it’s not. articles.title: Bengaluru man pays Rs 90,000 for Country Vacations holiday membership, seeks cancellation within six weeks without using any benefits; NCDRC calls company's reliance on 'no-refund' clause 'patently unfair and unjust' and orders full refund with 6% interest
articles.summary: NEW DELHI/BENGALURU: A Bengaluru man who paid Rs 90,000 for a long-term holiday membership but sought to cancel it within six weeks without using any of
articles.body: NEW DELHI/BENGALURU: A Bengaluru man who paid Rs 90,000 for a long-term holiday membership but sought to cancel it within six weeks without using any of its benefits is entitled to a refund, the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) has ruled. The commission held that refusing to cancel the membership by citing a contractual 'no-refund' clause, despite the consumer having availed no facilities, amounted to unfair and unjust conduct.Dismissing a revision petition filed by Country Vacations and Country Club (India) Ltd, the NCDRC upheld an order of the Karnataka State Consumer Commission directing the companies to refund the membership fee with 6% annual interest and pay Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs.The complaint was filed by Sangeeth Bhadran, who received a promotional call from Country Vacations on December 2, 2013, offering holiday and vacation facilities and inviting him to visit its office. Five days later, Bhadran visited the company's Bengaluru office and signed a membership purchase agreement after being offered holiday benefits, accommodation facilities and discounts. He paid Rs 90,000 for the membership.However, he later found that the benefits described during the promotional interaction did not match the actual terms and conditions of the agreement. He also alleged that he had been assured that maintenance charges would not apply to facilities he did not use. After examining the agreement, Bhadran sought cancellation and a refund of his money. Despite repeated emails, telephone calls and personal visits, the companies allegedly refused to cancel the membership or return the amount.He subsequently approached the III Additional Bangalore Urban District Consumer Forum, which dismissed his complaint, finding no deficiency in service or unfair trade practice. Bhadran challenged the decision before the Karnataka State Consumer Commission, which ruled in his favour and directed the companies to refund Rs 90,000 with 6% annual interest from the date of filing the complaint until payment. It also awarded him Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs.Country Vacations and Country Club then approached the NCDRC, arguing that Bhadran had voluntarily entered into the agreement after understanding its terms, including the non-refundable nature of the membership fee. The companies said membership cards and gift vouchers had been issued to him, but he had neither attempted to use the holiday facilities nor paid the mandatory annual maintenance charges. They denied any misrepresentation or deficiency in service and argued that he had failed to produce evidence to support his allegations.The NCDRC, however, observed that Bhadran's failure to use the membership facilities could not, by itself, absolve the companies of unfair conduct or validate one-sided contractual terms. It noted that he had been invited to the office, where the membership benefits were presented and the agreement signed on the same day. Within approximately one-and-a-half months, without availing any benefits, he sought to withdraw from the long-term arrangement. The commission held that refusing a refund by relying on the 'no-refund' clause, while continuing to impose an annual maintenance liability under the agreement was 'patently unfair and unjust'.It observed that the companies could perhaps have deducted a proportionate amount for the one-and-a-half-month period, along with reasonable administrative charges or an earnest amount, before returning the balance. The commission said retaining the entire membership fee despite the consumer having availed no benefits would result in unjust and disproportionate enrichment of the companies.Finding no jurisdictional or other error in the Karnataka State Consumer Commission's order, the NCDRC dismissed the revision petition. articles.title: Waymo suspends driverless freeway rides across US after California ban
articles.summary: California authorities have declared self-driving cars an ‘imminent hazard to public safety’ after traffic incidents.
articles.body:
Waymo has paused its driverless taxi services on freeways across the United States after California temporarily banned the ride-hailing platform on the state’s highways over safety concerns.

A spokesperson for the California-based company – a subsidiary of Alphabet, Google’s parent company – said it has “temporarily restricted commercial freeway rides in all markets where we operate that service”, but it is “continuing freeway testing with trained autonomous specialists behind the wheel”.

Waymo implemented the suspension last Wednesday, according to the spokesperson, but they did not say how long it would last.

Along with California, the driverless vehicles will pause highway services in Phoenix, Austin and Miami. Waymo offers rides on city streets in areas including Las Vegas, Dallas and Denver.

The spokesperson said the suspension would allow the company to “evaluate our performance” following incidents in California and that it prioritises safety.

One incident on November 6 went viral after video captured on a San Francisco highway showed a Waymo vehicle speeding towards and attempting to pass two police cars, even as their lights were flashing in an intentional bid to slow traffic.

The officers were driving behind a slow-moving construction truck.

The episode led the California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) to temporarily ban Waymo vehicles from its highways, effective from November 11.

The DMV, which is responsible for road safety, said its decision was also prompted by a November 5 incident, when three Waymo autonomous vehicles drove into a construction zone in the San Francisco Bay Area.

Waymo said the construction zone incident did not result in injuries or collisions.

DMV spokesman Jonathan Groveman said in a statement that “similar incidents” occurred on May 18.

“The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,” he said.

The restrictions “will remain in place until Waymo demonstrates … it has taken effective corrective actions”, the statement read.

Waymo completes half a million trips each week and says it has demonstrated a 95 percent reduction in serious crashes as compared with human-driven vehicles.

It has been testing its vehicles in London since 2016, and has plans to expand into Munich and Madrid in 2027.

articles.title: Corby must 'show authentic voice' in Town of Culture bid
articles.summary: 'Little Scotland' is one of 15 to make the medium category shortlist for Town of Culture 2028.
articles.body:
Corby will need to showcase its "authentic voice" and the aspirations of locals in its bid to be crowned Town of Culture 2028, the head judge of the competition Sir Phil Redmond has said.

The Grange Hill and Brookside creator visited the Northamptonshire town on Monday for an informal visit, where he was shown around several locations including Corby Cube, Adrenaline Alley and Chapel Gym.

"We're looking for a place that wants to celebrate who they are," said Sir Phil.

[That is] proud of what they are and who want other people to come and see what they are."

The deadline for bid submissions for the UK Town of Culture 2028 competition is 30 November.

Corby is one of 15 towns to have made the shortlist in the medium towns category, alongside Great Yarmouth in Norfolk, Leith in Scotland, and Pontypridd and Port Talbot in Wales.

The town received £60,000 to develop its full bid, which will be assessed by an independent judging panel.

Sir Phil told the BBC that judges of the competition are looking for the town's "authentic voice" in the bid.

"[It is] purely about celebrating what you've got and who you are, and the enthusiasm, the talent, the ambitions [and] the aspirations of the people," he said.

"That's coming over very loud and clear this morning.

"To impress us, [they need to] do what they said on their bid, say that this is Corby, this [why it is] great, and this is why it should be Town of Culture."

Corby is known as Little Scotland , after thousands of Scots migrated to the town to work in the steelworks in the 1930s.

"I think the Scottish link has come over very loud and clear today, especially the two pipers [who] piped me in at the beginning, that was really good," Sir Phil said.

Sir Phil said the decision to choose a winner would be "hard".

"I think each town would be able to do a really good [job] but there can only be one winner and that's the tough side of my job.

"[With] cities that have not made City of Culture there's nothing particularly wrong it's just that somewhere else offered something different.

"Coming and meeting the people, seeing everybody within the community and seeing that enthusiasm is the great side of my job, but it'll all come down to that big decision at the end," he added.

The overall winner will be announced early next year.
